study_type_evidence.quote: After 4 h fasting (ad libitum water intake), mice were subcutaneously injected with 50 mg/kg TIPP.
The stability of TIPP in processed murine plasma samples was studied under four different conditions (Table 4).
RBL-2H3 cells were seeded in a 35 mm diameter dish at 8 × 105 cells and treated with 200 μg/mL TIPP

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: female BALB/c mice, 6-8 weeks old, from Beijing Vital River Laboratory Animal Technology
in_vivo_species.quote: Female BALB/c mice (6–8 weeks old) were purchased from Beijing Vital River Laboratory Animal Technology Co., Ltd.

ex_vivo_detail: Blank murine (BALB/c mouse) plasma was drawn and then spiked with TIPP to assess matrix stability and extraction recovery: TIPP remained stable for 4 h at room temperature, 24 h at 4 °C in the autosampler, three freeze-thaw cycles and four weeks at -80 °C, with extraction recovery 41.1-42.6%. Degradation of TIPP in plasma was also compared against aqueous solution during protein-precipitation optimisation ('the intensity decreased significantly in plasma under the same conditions'), and dithiothreitol was required as a stabiliser to prevent cross-linking of the cysteine thiol in the plasma matrix.
in_vitro_detail: RBL-2H3 rat basophilic leukaemia cells incubated with 200 μg/mL TIPP: concentration-time profiles in culture supernatant, cell lysate and the final PBS rinse were measured by LC-MS/MS, an intracellular degradation half-life of 5.596 min was fitted after switching to TIPP-free medium, FITC-TIPP uptake was visualised by confocal microscopy, and anti-degranulation activity was assessed against IgE/DNP-HSA challenge (beta-hexosaminidase, histamine, IL-4).

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Plasma concentration-time profile after 50 mg/kg subcutaneous administration of TIPP (mean ± SD, n = 8 at each time point).
concentration_time_figure.note: Mouse plasma concentration versus time over 0.5-40 min after a single subcutaneous dose. Figure 5a-c additionally plot TIPP concentration versus time in RBL-2H3 cell culture supernatant and cell lysate, and the decline of intracellular TIPP after switching to TIPP-free medium (in vitro).

bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS: Shimadzu Nexera X2 LC with a Thermo Hypersil Gold C18 column (2.1 × 100 mm, 5 μm), gradient 0.1% formic acid in water/acetonitrile, coupled to an API 5500 Q trap with Turbo Ion Spray ESI in positive multiple-reaction-monitoring mode; validated to FDA bioanalytical guidelines
bioanalytical_quote: MS detection was performed using API 5500 Q trap mass spectrometer (Applied Biosystems, Waltham, MA, USA) equipped with a Turbo Ion SprayTM ESI source
notes: Fully specified PK dataset (Table 5): AUC(0-t) 7982.05 ± 1488.44 μg/L×min, AUC(0-∞) 8182.81 ± 1529.9 μg/L×min, MRT(0-t) 11.32 ± 1.29 min, MRT(0-∞) 12.53 ± 1.46 min, t1/2 5.99 ± 1.82 min, Tmax 10.00 ± 0.00 min, CL/F 6.34 ± 1.45 L/min/kg, Vd/F 54.39 ± 20.95 L/kg, Cmax 623.00 ± 67.13 μg/L. half_life_phase is 'elimination' on the authors' own naming - verbatim Results quote: 'The AUC, elimination half-life (t1/2), peak concentration (Tmax), maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), mean residence time (MRT), apparent volume of distribution (Vd/F), and apparent clearance rate (CL/F) were calculated using STATA software (Table 5)'. No absorption half-life is reported; the only absorption descriptor is Tmax = 10 min, so half_life_absorption is 'not reported' and the 10 min value is kept in tmax, not in half_life. No rate constants are printed, so no ln2/k conversion was needed or performed. Note the Methods say t1/2 'was calculated from C0 to C40' and that the Analysis section says a non-compartmental model (DAS 2.0) was used while the PK Methods say CL/F and Vd/F came from a first-order one-compartment model - this internal inconsistency is recorded but not resolved. Unit check: the Results text writes Cmax as '623 ng/mL' and the Discussion and Table 5 as '623 μg/L'; these are numerically identical, so there is no discrepancy. Separate in vitro value, deliberately NOT placed in the agent PK fields: intracellular TIPP in RBL-2H3 cells declined with 't1/2 = 5.596 min' after removal of extracellular peptide - that is a cellular efflux/degradation half-life, not a plasma half-life. Intravenous PK was attempted but not reported ('Due to rapid elimination after intravenous injection (data not shown)'). Anti-DNP-IgE (0.2 μg/mL), DNP-HSA (1 μg/mL), DTT, L-AA and PMSF were in vitro sensitising, challenge or stabiliser reagents rather than administered test substances and were not given agent objects.
